recipes.label: How did you hear about this job?*
Could you please list the standard and widespread ML techniques you're most comfortable with*
recipes.value: Supervised and unsupervised learning, deep learning, and transformers day to day: classification, metric learning, and sequence models in PyTorch. On the LLM side, retrieval-augmented generation, PEFT/LoRA fine-tuning, quantisation (FP8, 4-bit) and systematic evaluation. Also computer vision (CNNs, vision-language models) and NLP, plus feature engineering, A/B testing and statistical modelling on the analysis side.

recipes.label: Briefly describe a project where you had to deploy ML models serving real-time responses on large scale*
recipes.value: At Aria I deployed Phi-3 Vision behind vLLM for a document-understanding pipeline serving real-time requests at 20 ms median latency, parsing millions of scientific PDFs. The work was in batching and quantisation: FP8 weights, tuned concurrency, and a Qdrant hybrid-retrieval backbone (BGE-M3 dense, ColBERT, bm42 sparse) so retrieval stayed inside the latency budget.
